pool_ledger_sum_proof.formula: U_coin(t) = sum_p max(0, floor((R_p + Delta_p(t))/10^12) - H_p)
pool_ledger_sum_proof.delta_formula: Delta_p=0 if dt<=0 or a_p=0 or E=0; otherwise floor(E*dt*a_p/A). For missing share assume share>0, which only overestimates actual release when actual share=0.
pool_ledger_sum_proof.claim: If actual shared-vault balance >= U_coin(t), cash suffices for every reward payment permitted by the released pool budgets at the snapshot, without reading user positions.
basis: Each successful withdraw_reward(amount) increments H_p then requires H_p<=floor(R_p/10^12); no user payout can exceed its pool released budget.

All per-pool reward accounts are indexed by Rewarder.pools. add_pool pushes a new zero-initialized entry. Inspected current module has no remove_pool/pop/remove_rewarder/reset release/harvest function. Thus completed same-checkpoint lists contain every current registered pool reward budget.
update_rewarder and set_pool settle all pools using old emission/allocation before changing parameters; current E, a, A apply after each account last_reward_time.
Pool share zero suppresses incremental release; assuming positive share is conservative for a payment upper bound.

Only withdraw_reward performs ordinary user payment from the private manager vault. deposit_rewarder only adds; emergent_withdraw requires AdminCap and its current cash effect is reflected in the snapshot. Future administrative withdrawal belongs permission analysis.
Budget summation is per coin; no cross-coin offset. Floor each pool separately, clamp deficits separately, and only then sum.
pool_ledger_sum_proof.scope_limit: Current released payment budgets, not future infinite emissions or an exact sum of every user reward entitlement. An inconsistent historical allocation that exceeds a pool payment cap would be a code/allocation issue, not evidence of missing vault cash; no fresh code audit performed.

definitions.S: All outstanding XCETUS supply from the TreasuryCap; includes tokens subject to outstanding redemption requests until burned
definitions.L: Global accumulator of original XCETUS quantities reserved by redemption requests, not the amount of CETUS still in main custody
definitions.B: LockUpManager.balance, CETUS held in main manager
definitions.U: S-L; XCETUS units not already reserved by requests; can request future CETUS payout up to 1:1 under current maximum schedule
definitions.x_i: Original XCETUS quantity of active redemption request i, LockInfo.xcetus_amount
definitions.p_i: CETUS cash fixed at request creation and transferred out of main into corresponding lock coin, LockInfo.cetus_amount
definitions.P: Sum of LockInfo.cetus_amount for applicable live redemption requests. Equality to physical lock-coin balances requires live-object correspondence, particularly for legacy V1 objects with public destruction.
definitions.D: Sum of x_i-p_i for applicable live requests. Protocol discount transfer required by normal locking wrappers, not additional user cash entitlement. An orphaned legacy LockInfo after direct V1 helper consumption must not automatically count as an executable request.
definitions.E: LockUpManager.extra_treasury; protocol treasury cash, excluded from user principal funding

equations.counterConsistency: Current normal wrappers increment/decrement L with original x_i and add/remove corresponding LockInfo records; current code alone does not certify the correspondence of every old record to a still-live lock coin.
equations.managerRequirement: B >= U+D = (S-L)+D = S-P, sufficient for simultaneous unrequested face-value principal and required pending-discount settlement under current wrapper paths
equations.grossUserOnlyDiagnostic: B-U > 0 is observed, but does not quantify D or prove all wrapper redemptions can complete
equations.snapshotGap: B-U = 161997.428431689 CETUS; complete manager requirement would require D <= this amount; D is unobserved, so no deficit or surplus is asserted

normalTransitions.restriction: Only available_value can burn; requires AdminCap plus mutable owner VeNFT

confirmed: convert takes n CETUS into main before minting n XCETUS
request creation fixes p<=x, transfers p from main into a lock coin and records x,p and the lock id
current cancel/redeem wrappers bind lock id, VeNFT id and CETUS value to LockInfo; cancellation requires pre-maturity
main funds are not a yield reward pool; ordinary treasury withdrawal accesses extra only
all inspected current normal transitions preserve Q; available-only administrative token burning can increase Q
dividend corrections affect dividend entitlement; available_value for principal redemption uses raw xcetus_amount minus lock_amount
V2 helper actually stores Balance<CETUS> in LockedCoinV2; value() reads that balance, and lock_time() returns locked_until_time
V2 creation, unlock and cancellation-destruction helpers are public(friend); arbitrary external user calls cannot independently unlock or destroy V2
V2 unlock requires locked_until_time <= Clock, deletes the owned lock coin and transfers all its cash to tx_context::sender

Cancellation is a valid normal path before maturity: locking::cancel_redeem_lock_v2 requires lock_time > now, verifies VeNFT id, actual coin value and lock id, removes request, decreases L and returns its actual balance to main. It does not burn S or settle D.

Current normal V2 redemption does not need a keeper, oracle or reinvestment. It does require caller-owned lock coin plus VeNFT, package gate, maturity, matching record, token burn and main balance sufficient for that request discount transfer; any later abort reverts helper cash transfer atomically.

Legacy V1 helper unlock_coin and destory_lock are public. Mature V1 coins can be independently unlocked without wrapper; destory_lock has no time check and can return the contained balance to the object owner without wrapper bookkeeping. This does not prove any active old objects exist, unauthorized theft or repeat withdrawal.
Current locking::redeem_lock V1 creation entry aborts; newly requested redemption uses V2. Existing old V1 cancel/redeem wrappers are still present.
Positive B-U remains confirmed, but main free surplus and complete wrapper funding require live-request D; no blanket U classification is warranted for already verified accounting properties.

v2.storage: LockedCoinV2<T> has key only, containing UID, Balance<T>, locked_start_time and locked_until_time
v2.creation: public(friend); end>start; converts supplied Coin into the same Balance and transfers newly created owned lock coin to supplied recipient. locking passes tx sender and current/end timestamps.
v2.value: public; reads balance::value from actual contained cash
v2.unlock: public(friend); requires end<=now; deletes object and transfers entire contained coin to tx sender; returns consumed object ID
v2.cancel: public(friend) destroy_for_cancel returns actual balance and consumed object ID without its own time check; the external locking wrapper supplies strict pre-maturity and binding checks

v1.ownership: Both consume the owned lock object; public visibility does not permit consuming another user-owned object without ownership authorization

early.individualFormula: D=1e9 (local SDK); P_i=purchase, w_i=protected purchase. Oversubscribed: refund_i=floor((R-H)*(P_i-w_i)/(R-W)); sale_i=floor(w_i*D/price)+floor((sale_total-floor(W*D/price))*(P_i-w_i)/(R-W)).
early.confirmed: Closed for the selected already-settled successful pool under the archived deployed code: current user reserves cover all remaining contract-defined sale and refund obligations by conservation and downward rounding. Precise debt totals are not stored at pool level; no per-user sum was performed. This does not create a score or generalize to other pools.

coverageProof.units: All formulas below use integer coin raw units.
coverageProof.protectedAggregate: WhiteList.purchase_total starts at 0; increse_white_list_purchase_total subtracts the old per-user protected amount, updates it by capped purchase increment, then adds the new amount. Removing a user requires protected amount=0; administrative changes are gated to initialization. Thus W=sum w_i, 0<=w_i<=p_i, R=sum p_i.
coverageProof.rounding: utils::math_u128_mul_div_to_u64 uses checked nonzero denominator, checked multiplication, integer Div and CastU64, hence floor for nonnegative values; overflow aborts rather than creating a payout.
coverageProof.saleAllocationProof: Let A=floor(W*D/price), T=R-W>0. Sum floor(w_i*D/price)<=A; sum floor((sale_total-A)*(p_i-w_i)/T)<=sale_total-A. Therefore total sale liabilities<=sale_total. Current sale_total*D/price relation and all allocation inputs are frozen after purchase stage.
coverageProof.refundAllocationProof: Sum floor((R-H)*(p_i-w_i)/(R-W))<=R-H. The p_i=w_i special branch has zero refund and its floor(w_i*D/price) sale allocation is consistent.
coverageProof.cashPartition: Successful settlement reserves sale_total for purchasers and R-H for refunds; owner-only unused_sale and harvest_raise are separate. Owner withdrawals reduce the same owner amount and reset it to zero, so user reserve is invariant under owner withdrawals. Claims subtract exactly the paid amounts.
coverageProof.singlePayment: Pool ID must match PurchaseMark. One mark is created per sender per pool. PurchaseMark has key but no store/copy, and the module only initially transfers it to that sender. Claim requires obtain_sale_amount=0 and used_raise_amount=purchase_total, then records the sale and purchased-minus-refund. Any positive payout makes that condition false; a possible repeated zero/zero payout cannot drain cash.
coverageProof.qualification: Zero here is the proved positive funding shortfall under the stated code invariant, not zero liability and not an assessment score. Existing valid receipt and normal allowed claim path remain necessary.

early.macroInvariant: sum remaining sale claims <= sale_coin-unused_sale; sum remaining SUI refunds <= raise_coin-harvest_raise. Successful settlement partitions inventory; user claims debit exact payout, owner sale/raise withdrawals debit matching unused_sale/harvest_raise only.

oversubscribed.individualFormula: D=1e18 (local SDK); u_i=w_i+(p_i-w_i)*(K-W)/(R-W); NAVX claim_i=floor(u_i*D/price); used_raise_i=ceil(u_i); refund_i=p_i-ceil(u_i).
oversubscribed.confirmed: Closed for the selected already-ended oversubscribed successful pool under archived deployed code: current NAVX and SUI cash cover remaining contract-defined redemption obligations by conservation. Emergency deposits can make cash exceed debt, so exact remaining debt cannot be reverse-inferred from cash. No per-user sum or score was produced.

coverageProof.protectedAggregate: update_for_purchase caps each protected increment by individual remaining limit, global remaining protection and purchase amount; caller adds this exact increment to white_list.protection_limit_used. Thus W=sum w_i and R=sum p_i. Changes to whitelist limits are restricted to initialization.
coverageProof.rounding: full_math_u64/u128 use full-width multiplication; floor is integer division, ceil is (product+denominator-1)/denominator. Pool uses floor for sale allocation and ceil for used raise. The exact price denominator 1e18 and liquidity denominator 1e6 are in the deployed pool constants.
coverageProof.allocationProof: sum u_i=K. Here K*1e18/price=total_supply exactly. Therefore sum sale_i<=total_supply and sum refund_i=R-sum ceil(u_i)<=R-K. The global protection total W<K and R> K in the selected state, so denominators and residual allocations are valid.
coverageProof.cashPartition: create deposits total_supply plus reserved liquidity sale. Purchase adds full purchased raise. Actual CLMM draw is stored in liquidity_used_*; success owner withdrawal is K-liquidity_used_raise and zero sale in this oversubscribed pool. With sale liquidity reserve exactly consumed in selected state, cash after these steps is at least total_supply for sale entitlements and R-K for refunds, minus exactly already-paid user claims. Emergency deposits only add cash without increasing rights.
coverageProof.singlePaymentAndBinding: Outer redeem checks certificate pool ID and !is_redeemed; update_for_redeem sets certificate and sender table record is_redeemed=true and records sale/used; refunded_raise_amount is purchased-used. create limits one certificate per sender, and transfer_purchase_certificate_to checks table certificate ID matches the exact certificate. Certificate has key without store/copy, so it cannot be externally forged, copied or freely transferred; the only provided transfer binds the same table owner.
coverageProof.ownerWithdrawalClosed: is_withdrawn=true causes further owner withdrawal to abort. Current is_liquidity_injected=true and exact reserved NAVX liquidity already consumed.
coverageProof.qualification: This proves cash coverage bounds, not exact unclaimed totals, user eligibility of a chosen receipt, or a score. It is limited to this pool and same-checkpoint code/state.

oversubscribed.macroInvariant: Sum NAVX allocations <= total_supply; sum refunds <= R-K. Liquidity draws only the reserved liquidity inventory. Owner success withdrawal takes K-liquidity_used_raise and zero sale in oversubscription, only once. Already-paid claims debit pool inventory. Emergency deposits only add assets.

evidence.note: Exact deployed helper disassembly checked against pool disassembly; local SDK is corroboration only. No transaction or per-user queries.

launchpad.nextPointReads: None required to prove selected-pool cash coverage under these contract invariants. Exact outstanding liability totals require a per-user aggregate or separate authenticated accumulator, neither needed for the upper-bound coverage proof nor collected here.

Do not leave both as U only because no exact per-user debt sum was obtained; do not convert this into a score without the agreed module rule.
